related_questions.question: What's the quickest way to get rid of COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: The fastest way to recover from COVID-19 involves a combination of rest, over-the-counter medications for symptom relief, and potentially antiviral treatments if you are at high risk for severe illness. While there's no single "quick fix," these strategies can help your body clear the virus more efficiently.
snippet_highlighted_words: a combination of rest, over-the-counter medications for symptom relief, and potentially antiviral treatments if you are at high risk for severe illness

text_blocks.snippet: 1. Prioritize Rest: Getting adequate sleep (more than the recommended 7-9 hours for adults) is crucial for your immune system to function optimally and fight off the virus, according to UnityPoint Health.
2. Manage Symptoms with Over-the-Counter Medications: Medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help reduce fever and body aches, making you more comfortable and allowing you to rest.

3. Consider Antiviral Treatments if Eligible: If you are at higher risk for severe COVID-19, antiviral medications like Paxlovid can help reduce the severity and duration of your illness, according to the CDC. Consult with a healthcare provider to determine if you are eligible for these treatments.
4. Monitor Your Health: Regularly check for any worsening symptoms and seek immediate medical attention if you experience a medical emergency, says UnityPoint Health.
5. Prevent Further Spread: Continue to isolate yourself, wear a mask when around others, and avoid sharing items like dishes and towels to prevent transmission, notes UnityPoint Health.

related_questions.question: Why do I keep getting COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: You may be getting COVID repeatedly due to several factors, including waning immunity from previous infections or vaccinations, exposure to new variants, and the nature of the virus itself. Even if you've had COVID before, it doesn't guarantee lifelong immunity, and you can still contract the virus again.
snippet_highlighted_words: waning immunity from previous infections or vaccinations, exposure to new variants, and the nature of the virus itself

list.title: Waning Immunity:
list.snippet: The protection you get from previous COVID-19 infections or vaccinations can decrease over time. This means you become more susceptible to reinfection as your antibody levels drop.

list.title: New Variants:
list.snippet: New variants of the virus can emerge that are more contagious or better at evading immunity, making it easier to get infected even if you've been previously exposed to an older variant.

list.title: Exposure:
list.snippet: Frequent or high-risk exposure to the virus significantly increases your chances of getting infected, regardless of prior immunity.

list.title: Individual Factors:
list.snippet: Certain factors, like underlying health conditions or a weakened immune system, can make some people more vulnerable to reinfection.

list.title: Long COVID:
list.snippet: Repeated infections can increase the risk of developing long COVID, a condition where symptoms persist for weeks or months after the initial infection.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to remember that even with prior infections, taking precautions like vaccination, masking in crowded indoor spaces, and practicing good hygiene can help reduce your risk of getting COVID again.
